bulletin.title: KCMC Community Updates — October 20–25, 2026
bulletin.welcome: Called to love and serve. Worship, serve and share time together at KCMC. There is a place for you here!
notes: Sunday worship — 8:00 AM Front Porch Gospel, 9:15 AM Traditional Worship, and 10:30 AM Contemporary Worship. LaunchKids Children’s Church meets at 10:30 AM.
Friends of Faith Sunday Bible Study — Sundays at 10:20 AM in the Pairs & Spares Classroom. Becoming Like Jesus by Matt Chandler.
Thursday, October 22, 1:30 PM — Way Forward All Church Informational Meeting with Pastor Tony.
Return filled Pregnancy Life Line baby bottles by Sunday, October 25.

Saturday, October 31, 4:30–6:30 PM — Trunk or Treat in the church parking lot. Contact the church office about signing up a trunk; individually wrapped candy donations are needed at the office or in the lobby.
Saturday, November 14, 4:30 PM — Richard French Memorial Lasagna Dinner, Fellowship Hall. Tickets are $15 each.
For prayer or a conversation with a pastor, call the church office at 417-739-4395. Services are live-streamed on Facebook.

trunk-or-treat-2026.description: Bring the family for a bounce house, hot dogs, hot cider and a costume contest. Contact the church office about signing up a trunk, decorating your vehicle and helping distribute candy. Individually wrapped candy donations may be dropped off at the church office or in the lobby. All are welcome.

trunk-volunteers-20261014.body: Help us reach at least 30 decorated trunks! Sign up to bring your vehicle and welcome children and families. The pastors have promised a party for participants if we reach 30 trunks. Volunteers should arrive by 3:30 PM on October 31 to park and decorate. Plan for approximately 200 children: about 200 individually wrapped treats for one each, or 400 for two each. Use commercially packaged, individually wrapped treats. Extra candy is available, and the church can provide candy if purchasing it is a burden. Drop off donated candy at the church office or in the lobby. Keep decorations and optional costumes family-friendly and not frightening; an adult volunteer costume contest is planned. Keep walkways clear and cords secure. Keep vehicles parked until the event is over and families have cleared the area. Smile, welcome each child and be patient with shy visitors. Contact the church office with questions. Contact the church office about signing up a trunk. The public event runs October 31, 4:30–6:30 PM in the church parking lot, with a bounce house, hot dogs, hot cider and a costume contest.
